citation: 'Residence for Edward F. Robbins, 2126 Prairie Ave., Chicago. Mann, MacNeille and Lindeberg, Architects, New York and Chicago.' Plate, The Inland Architect and News Record, vol. XLV no. 4 (May 1905); Inland Architect Press.
author: unknown photographer; Mann, MacNeille & Lindeberg (architects of the Robbins house); Inland Architect Press
describes_date: the finished house before May 1905, photographed with the trees bare (late 1904 or early 1905); the plate dates the completed house no earlier than its own printing allows, and says nothing about July 1904

locator: The whole leaf: the Robbins front at 2126 Prairie square-on from the east walk, filling the plate between the brick flank of its southern neighbour at the left and the bracketed brick front of its northern neighbour at the right.
rights_note: Published in the United States in 1905: public domain by date.
access_notes: Read 2026-11-22 (T-3721) from the image store's display copies: dw-inland-1905-05-robbins-2126-plate.jpg, 2400 x 1634 px, sha256 7442ccceb5f5df56decaa6fe845d90d7da028e044c24bb9b8ccea045ef19d44a, and a20-aic-ia-robbins-plate.jpg, 1056 x 733 px, sha256 4c3a177f09c9225da56dc92ddc225bdb719213cfd6cafdcbf596070601ee049b. Neither is committed here. The two are one photograph. Measured on the larger copy at about 95 px a metre of the front (the front's 12.19 m on sheet 35 of the 1911 Sanborn over its 1160 px), square-on, so heights and widths on the front's plane read within about 0.1 m; no camera is solved yet (T-3722).
note: The finished front: three storeys of brick over a pale marble basement, five bays with a fanlit door in the middle. Principal-storey sash under flat marble lintels with a keystone, marble panels between the storeys, the second storey's sash rising to a marble entablature whose architrave is carried on four Ionic pilaster heads between the bays, a dentil course and a pale sill band over it, an attic storey of five short sash with eared marble dressings, and a moulded cornice on blocks at a flat top. Two end chimneys stand behind the cornice. Before the front a marble-capped area wall with an iron railing on it, two brick gate piers with ball finials at the walk, a brick wall with a ball-topped pier returned north and a scrolled marble stop at the south corner.
